chunks: About the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Allah takes the souls at the time of their death.”
And about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Say: the Angel of Death, who has been entrusted with you, will take you.”
And about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Those whom the angels take while they are pure.”
And: “Those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves.”
And about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Our messengers took him.”
And about His saying, Mighty and Majestic: “And if you could see when the angels take those who disbelieved.”
And there may die in a single hour, across all regions, a number that none can enumerate except Allah, Mighty and Majestic; so how is this?

He said: “Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has appointed for the Angel of Death helpers from among the angels who seize the souls, like the chief of police who has helpers from among men and sends them in his affairs. So the angels take them, and the Angel of Death takes them from the angels along with what he himself seizes, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, takes it from the Angel of Death.”

key_terms.أَعْوَانًا: helpers or assistants appointed for a task
key_terms.الْأَرْوَاحَ: the spirits that are seized at death
key_terms.الْأَنْفُسَ: the souls or selves of human beings
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةُ: the angels who assist in taking souls
key_terms.مَلَكُ الْمَوْتِ: the Angel of Death charged with receiving souls
key_terms.يَتَوَفَّى: takes fully, referring here to taking the soul at death

ai.seo_question: How do the Qur'anic verses about Allah, the Angel of Death, and the angels taking souls fit together?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic verses that variously attribute the taking of souls to Allah, the Angel of Death, and the angels. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام clarifies that these descriptions are all true: the angels assist, Malak al-Mawt receives, and ultimately Allah is the true taker of souls.
